reviewer_comment: R2-2: What about differences is "information" storage needs for your approach compared to others?
scope: Frozen primary Lorenz and CSTR models, Lh=M=20. No new scientific fitting or checkpoint changes.
input: First original training trajectory for each system, common origins 20..275; original train-fitted normalization. No test data.
inference_probe: All neural and RBF inference on same GPU in float64. Neural code is unchanged except tensor dtype. RBF inference-only adapter validated against native float64 NumPy equations. This is a standardized allocation comparison, not native-precision memory or prediction-accuracy evidence.
training_probe: All neural stages use float64 for unified accounting; one warmup and three full-step allocation probes on disposable copies, weights restored before measurements. Native neural training was float32. RBF fit arrays are reported at float64 for N=47500; no whole-fit peak or Adam-stage claim.
inference_peak_definition: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated minus resident model/input allocation immediately before rollout; includes outputs, diagnostic copies and auxiliary tensors; excludes caching-reserved memory, CUDA context, host dataset and Python metadata.
amendment_reason: Lorenz Markov RBF float32 H60 conversion failed the fixed output agreement threshold (max_abs_error=0.012777414307856838, RMS=0.00019661577631099078). Preserve pilot results; compare all models at float64 without downcasting the RBF models. No threshold relaxed and no model retrained.
